exposure: Environmental antibiotics (tetracycline, sulfamonomethoxine, doxycycline, lincomycin, and 6 other unspecified antibiotics in urine samples)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 1855 obese and 1875 randomly selected control primary school students.
finding: Low- to middle-level exposures to certain environmental antibiotics, specifically tetracycline, sulfamonomethoxine, doxycycline, and lincomycin, were associated with an increased risk of childhood obesity, especially in boys, with non-linear associations observed.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken in primary school students.
